key_insight: PR3DICTR is a modular, open-access framework built on PyTorch and MONAI that standardizes training and evaluation for 3D medical image classification and outcome prediction, enabling faster, reproducible model development.
problem_solved: Addresses fragmentation and high engineering overhead in 3D medical imaging research by providing a standardized, flexible platform that unifies data handling, preprocessing, model training, and evaluation to improve reproducibility and accelerate experimentation.
method: Modular pipeline design: interchangeable components for data loading, preprocessing/augmentation, model architectures, and training loops to support detection and outcome prediction workflows.
Built on community standards (PyTorch + MONAI) with configurable, reproducible training recipes and evaluation metrics to encourage sharing and benchmarking.
Open-access tooling and examples that reduce engineering effort and promote rapid prototyping of 3D imaging models.
impact: Makes 3D medical imaging research more accessible and reproducible for AI/ML practitioners, reducing implementation friction and enabling consistent benchmarking and faster translation from prototype to validation.
visual_elements: High-level pipeline diagram (Data → Preprocessing/Augmentation → Model Zoo → Training → Evaluation)
Modularity infographic showing interchangeable components (loaders, transforms, models, loss/metrics)
Before/after example: 3D volume with predicted detections/heatmap overlays
Bar chart or table comparing time-to-prototype, reproducibility, or benchmark results vs ad-hoc implementations
paper_title: PR3DICTR: A modular AI framework for medical 3D image-based detection and outcome prediction
paper_authors: Daniel C. MacRae, Luuk van der Hoek, Robert van der Wal, Suzanne P. M. de Vette, Hendrike Neh
